Interaction: Authorization code record

1. Potential Excessive Resource Consumption for Authenticate user or Session store  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Denial Of Service
Description:Does Authenticate user or Session store take explicit steps to control resource consumption? Resource consumption attacks can be hard to deal with, and there are times that it makes sense to let the OS do the job. Be careful that your resource requests don't deadlock, and that they do timeout.
Justification:Codes are single-use and expire with the client login timeout, and the number of authentication sessions per browser session is capped. Cache sizing is a deployment setting.

2. Spoofing of Destination Data Store Session store  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Spoofing
Description:Session store may be spoofed by an attacker and this may lead to data being written to the attacker's target instead of Session store. Consider using a standard authentication mechanism to identify the destination data store.
Justification:The session store is Keycloak&#39;s embedded Infinispan cache, persisted to the Keycloak database. Cluster traffic between nodes is TLS-encrypted by default, and nodes need the cluster certificate stored in the database to join.

3. Spoofing the Authenticate user Process  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Spoofing
Description:Authenticate user may be spoofed by an attacker and this may lead to unauthorized access to Session store. Consider using a standard authentication mechanism to identify the source process.
Justification:Only Keycloak nodes write to the session store. The session store is Keycloak&#39;s embedded Infinispan cache, persisted to the Keycloak database. Cluster traffic between nodes is TLS-encrypted by default, and nodes need the cluster certificate stored in the database to join.

4. The Session store Data Store Could Be Corrupted  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Tampering
Description:Data flowing across Authorization code record may be tampered with by an attacker. This may lead to corruption of Session store. Ensure the integrity of the data flow to the data store.
Justification:The code record (PKCE challenge, redirect URI, user session) stays server-side and never passes through the browser. Changing it requires access to the cache or database, which only Keycloak nodes have. The session store is Keycloak&#39;s embedded Infinispan cache, persisted to the Keycloak database. Cluster traffic between nodes is TLS-encrypted by default, and nodes need the cluster certificate stored in the database to join.

5. Data Store Denies Session store Potentially Writing Data  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Repudiation
Description:Session store claims that it did not write data received from an entity on the other side of the trust boundary. Consider using logging or auditing to record the source, time, and summary of the received data.
Justification:Writes happen inside Keycloak as part of the request. Failures surface as server errors and error events. The LOGIN event records the code being issued.

6. Data Flow Sniffing  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Information Disclosure
Description:Data flowing across Authorization code record may be sniffed by an attacker. Depending on what type of data an attacker can read, it may be used to attack other parts of the system or simply be a disclosure of information leading to compliance violations. Consider encrypting the data flow.
Justification:Cache replication between nodes is TLS-encrypted by default. Persisted sessions travel over the JDBC connection, which needs TLS that Keycloak does not enforce; our deployment requires it.

7. Data Flow Authorization code record Is Potentially Interrupted  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Denial Of Service
Description:An external agent interrupts data flowing across a trust boundary in either direction.
Justification:If this flow is interrupted, no code, token, or session is issued, so the login fails closed and the user starts over.

8. Data Store Inaccessible  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Denial Of Service
Description:An external agent prevents access to a data store on the other side of the trust boundary.
Justification:If the store is unavailable, logins and token requests fail closed. Availability comes from database replication and a clustered cache.

Interaction: Authorization request

9. Spoofing the End user (browser) External Entity  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Spoofing
Description:End user (browser) may be spoofed by an attacker and this may lead to unauthorized access to Authenticate user. Consider using a standard authentication mechanism to identify the external entity.
Justification:The browser does not identify anyone by itself; Authenticate user establishes the user&#39;s identity through the login flow (Interaction 1). For this flow the parameters that matter are client_id and redirect_uri: Keycloak checks redirect_uri against the client&#39;s registered values, and PKCE (S256, required through the pkce-enforcer client policy) binds the code to whoever started the flow.

10. Cross Site Scripting  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Tampering
Description:The web server 'Authenticate user' could be a subject to a cross-site scripting attack because it does not sanitize untrusted input.
Justification:Login and broker pages are FreeMarker templates rendered with HTML auto-escaping (DefaultFreeMarkerProvider sets HTMLOutputFormat). Keycloak has shipped XSS fixes for these pages before, so stay on patched releases.

11. Elevation Using Impersonation  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:Authenticate user may be able to impersonate the context of End user (browser) in order to gain additional privilege.
Justification:The authorization request grants nothing until the user authenticates. Requested scopes are limited to the client scopes assigned to the client, and Full Scope Allowed is turned off (full-scope-disabled client policy) so tokens carry only the client&#39;s role scope mappings.

12. Cross Site Request Forgery  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:Cross-site request forgery (CSRF or XSRF) is a type of attack in which an attacker forces a user's browser to make a forged request to a vulnerable site by exploiting an existing trust relationship between the browser and the vulnerable web site. In a simple scenario, a user is logged in to web site A using a cookie as a credential. The other browses to web site B. Web site B returns a page with a hidden form that posts to web site A. Since the browser will carry the user's cookie to web site A, web site B now can take any action on web site A, for example, adding an admin to an account. The attack can be used to exploit any requests that the browser automatically authenticates, e.g. by session cookie, integrated authentication, IP whitelisting. The attack can be carried out in many ways such as by luring the victim to a site under control of the attacker, getting the user to click a link in a phishing email, or hacking a reputable web site that the victim will visit. The issue can only be resolved on the server side by requiring that all authenticated state-changing requests include an additional piece of secret payload (canary or CSRF token) which is known only to the legitimate web site and the browser and which is protected in transit through SSL/TLS. See the Forgery Protection property on the flow stencil for a list of mitigations.
Justification:Login form posts must carry the authentication session&#39;s session_code and tab_id along with the session cookie, so a forged cross-site post does not match. The OIDC state parameter protects the client side and must be checked by the client.

13. Elevation by Changing the Execution Flow in Authenticate user  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:An attacker may pass data into Authenticate user in order to change the flow of program execution within Authenticate user to the attacker's choosing.
Justification:Authentication flows are server-side and bound to the authentication session (session_code, execution, tab_id). A request that skips or replays a step is rejected and the flow restarts.

14. Authenticate user May be Subject to Elevation of Privilege Using Remote Code Execution  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:End user (browser) may be able to remotely execute code for Authenticate user.
Justification:The process parses parameters and tokens with standard libraries and never evaluates input as code. Keep Keycloak and its Java runtime patched and run it as an unprivileged user.

15. Data Flow Authorization request Is Potentially Interrupted  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Denial Of Service
Description:An external agent interrupts data flowing across a trust boundary in either direction.
Justification:Production mode refuses to start without HTTPS, which protects integrity. If this flow is interrupted, no code, token, or session is issued, so the login fails closed and the user starts over.

16. Potential Process Crash or Stop for Authenticate user  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Denial Of Service
Description:Authenticate user crashes, halts, stops or runs slowly; in all cases violating an availability metric.
Justification:Brute-force detection limits repeated login failures (Interaction 1). Keycloak has no per-client or per-IP rate limiting. Set http-max-queued-requests (no limit by default) so the server sheds load, and rate-limit by client and source IP at the reverse proxy. Run at least two nodes.

17. Potential Data Repudiation by Authenticate user  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Repudiation
Description:Authenticate user claims that it did not receive data from a source outside the trust boundary. Consider using logging or auditing to record the source, time, and summary of the received data.
Justification:Keycloak records LOGIN, LOGIN_ERROR and CODE_TO_TOKEN events with client_id, IP and session. Save events is off by default and only error events reach the server log, so our configuration turns it on and forwards events to the SIEM.

Interaction: Authorization response

18. Data Flow Authorization response Is Potentially Interrupted  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Denial Of Service
Description:An external agent interrupts data flowing across a trust boundary in either direction.
Justification:An undelivered code is never redeemed and expires with the client login timeout, 60 seconds by default; we set it under 10 seconds as Keycloak&#39;s threat docs advise. The user restarts login.

19. External Entity End user (browser) Potentially Denies Receiving Data  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Repudiation
Description:End user (browser) claims that it did not receive data from a process on the other side of the trust boundary. Consider using logging or auditing to record the source, time, and summary of the received data.
Justification:The LOGIN event records the code being issued, and a matching CODE_TO_TOKEN event (or its absence) shows whether the client redeemed it. Save events is off by default and only error events reach the server log, so our configuration turns it on and forwards events to the SIEM.

20. Spoofing of the End user (browser) External Destination Entity  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Spoofing
Description:End user (browser) may be spoofed by an attacker and this may lead to data being sent to the attacker's target instead of End user (browser). Consider using a standard authentication mechanism to identify the external entity.
Justification:This is the redirect URI manipulation threat. Register exact redirect URIs and enable the secure-redirect-uris-enforcer client policy (off by default) so wildcard and loopback registrations are rejected; a trailing * is otherwise honored as a prefix match. For confidential clients, the client secret stops an attacker from redeeming a misdelivered code.

Interaction: Broker login events

21. Potential Excessive Resource Consumption for Broker external login or Event store  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Denial Of Service
Description:Does Broker external login or Event store take explicit steps to control resource consumption? Resource consumption attacks can be hard to deal with, and there are times that it makes sense to let the OS do the job. Be careful that your resource requests don't deadlock, and that they do timeout.
Justification:Saved events have a configurable expiration, which bounds table growth; the SIEM keeps the long-term copy.

22. Potential SQL Injection Vulnerability for Event store  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Tampering
Description:SQL injection is an attack in which malicious code is inserted into strings that are later passed to an instance of SQL Server for parsing and execution. Any procedure that constructs SQL statements should be reviewed for injection vulnerabilities because SQL Server will execute all syntactically valid queries that it receives. Even parameterized data can be manipulated by a skilled and determined attacker.
Justification:Keycloak writes events through JPA/Hibernate with bound parameters, so request details are stored as values, not SQL.

23. Spoofing of Destination Data Store Event store  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Spoofing
Description:Event store may be spoofed by an attacker and this may lead to data being written to the attacker's target instead of Event store. Consider using a standard authentication mechanism to identify the destination data store.
Justification:The event store is the event table in the Keycloak database, written only when Save events is on. Keycloak reaches its database over the configured JDBC connection with a dedicated database account. Restrict that account to the Keycloak schema, require TLS with certificate validation on the JDBC URL (Keycloak does not enforce it), and keep the database on a segment only Keycloak nodes can reach.

Category:Tampering
Description:Data flowing across Broker login events may be tampered with by an attacker. This may lead to corruption of Event store. Ensure the integrity of the data flow to the data store.
Justification:Keycloak&#39;s event table is not tamper-evident; anyone with database write access can change it. Forward events to an append-only SIEM so the copy outside Keycloak is the record.

39. Broker external login Process Memory Tampered  [State: Not Applicable]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Tampering
Description:If Broker external login is given access to memory, such as shared memory or pointers, or is given the ability to control what Authenticate user executes (for example, passing back a function pointer.), then Broker external login can tamper with Authenticate user. Consider if the function could work with less access to memory, such as passing data rather than pointers. Copy in data provided, and then validate it.
Justification:Broker external login and Authenticate user are parts of the same Keycloak server process; the brokered identity is passed as an in-memory object, not across a trust boundary or shared memory.

51. Weak Access Control for a Resource  [State: Needs Investigation]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Information Disclosure
Description:Improper data protection of Keycloak database can allow an attacker to read information not intended for disclosure. Review authorization settings.
Justification:Largest gap in Interaction 3. The database holds client secrets as entered (compared directly, not hashed) unless they are vault references, plus each realm&#39;s generated signing keys, including the HMAC key that signs refresh tokens. Read access to the database is enough to forge tokens. Mitigations: vault references for client secrets, the java-keystore key provider instead of generated keys, restricted and audited database access, and encryption at rest.

96. Spoofing the Partner identity provider External Entity  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Spoofing
Description:Partner identity provider may be spoofed by an attacker and this may lead to unauthorized access to Broker external login. Consider using a standard authentication mechanism to identify the external entity.
Justification:Turn on Validate Signature with the partner&#39;s signing certificate pinned (or loaded from its metadata URL over TLS) and set Identity Provider Entity ID. Without them Keycloak accepts unsigned responses and skips the Issuer check, and Want Assertions Signed alone only checks that a signature is present. SP-initiated responses are bound to the request ID; leave the IDP-Initiated SSO URL name unset on partner-facing clients so unsolicited responses are refused.

98. Elevation Using Impersonation  [State: Needs Investigation]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:Broker external login may be able to impersonate the context of Partner identity provider in order to gain additional privilege.
Justification:The partner can assert group values that mappers turn into roles. Our design maps the partner only to a contractor role and uses Force sync mode so roles are re-checked each login, and 26.8.0 (CVE-2026-12388) blocks admin roles through mappers by default. Gap: anyone with manage-identity-providers can still create a mapper that grants non-admin business roles such as finance or payroll.

Category:Repudiation
Description:Broker external login claims that it did not receive data from a source outside the trust boundary. Consider using logging or auditing to record the source, time, and summary of the received data.
Justification:With Save events on, IDENTITY_PROVIDER_LOGIN, IDENTITY_PROVIDER_FIRST_LOGIN and FEDERATED_IDENTITY_LINK record brokered logins, and Store Tokens keeps the latest assertion. Gap: both are off by default, and role grants made by mappers emit no event, so a grant cannot be traced back to the assertion that caused it.

Even parameterized data can be manipulated by a skilled and determined attacker.

122. External Entity Client application Potentially Denies Receiving Data  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Repudiation
Description:Client application claims that it did not receive data from a process on the other side of the trust boundary. Consider using logging or auditing to record the source, time, and summary of the received data.
Justification:CODE_TO_TOKEN and REFRESH_TOKEN events record issuance to the client. Save events is off by default and only error events reach the server log, so our configuration turns it on and forwards events to the SIEM.

123. Data Flow Token response Is Potentially Interrupted  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Denial Of Service
Description:An external agent interrupts data flowing across a trust boundary in either direction.
Justification:The client retries with a refresh token or restarts login; the consumed code cannot be reused.

Interaction: User credentials and client registration

124. Weak Access Control for a Resource  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Information Disclosure
Description:Improper data protection of Keycloak database can allow an attacker to read information not intended for disclosure. Review authorization settings.
Justification:Holds password hashes, OTP secrets (Interaction 1) and each client&#39;s registered redirect URIs. Access is limited to the Keycloak database account and database administrators.

125. Persistent Cross Site Scripting  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Tampering
Description:The web server 'Authenticate user' could be a subject to a persistent cross-site scripting attack because it does not sanitize data store 'Keycloak database' inputs and output.
Justification:Stored values such as client names and user attributes are escaped on output. Login and broker pages are FreeMarker templates rendered with HTML auto-escaping (DefaultFreeMarkerProvider sets HTMLOutputFormat). Keycloak has shipped XSS fixes for these pages before, so stay on patched releases.

126. Cross Site Scripting  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Tampering
Description:The web server 'Authenticate user' could be a subject to a cross-site scripting attack because it does not sanitize untrusted input.
Justification:Client display names and user attributes from the database appear on login pages. Login and broker pages are FreeMarker templates rendered with HTML auto-escaping (DefaultFreeMarkerProvider sets HTMLOutputFormat). Keycloak has shipped XSS fixes for these pages before, so stay on patched releases.

127. Spoofing of Source Data Store Keycloak database  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Spoofing
Description:Keycloak database may be spoofed by an attacker and this may lead to incorrect data delivered to Authenticate user. Consider using a standard authentication mechanism to identify the source data store.
Justification:Keycloak reaches its database over the configured JDBC connection with a dedicated database account. Restrict that account to the Keycloak schema, require TLS with certificate validation on the JDBC URL (Keycloak does not enforce it), and keep the database on a segment only Keycloak nodes can reach. Shared with Interaction 1.

128. Spoofing the Authenticate user Process  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Spoofing
Description:Authenticate user may be spoofed by an attacker and this may lead to information disclosure by Keycloak database. Consider using a standard authentication mechanism to identify the destination process.
Justification:Keycloak reaches its database over the configured JDBC connection with a dedicated database account. Restrict that account to the Keycloak schema, require TLS with certificate validation on the JDBC URL (Keycloak does not enforce it), and keep the database on a segment only Keycloak nodes can reach.

129. Potential Data Repudiation by Authenticate user  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Repudiation
Description:Authenticate user claims that it did not receive data from a source outside the trust boundary. Consider using logging or auditing to record the source, time, and summary of the received data.
Justification:Admin events record client and user changes made through the admin API when enabled; database audit logging covers direct changes.

130. Potential Process Crash or Stop for Authenticate user  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Denial Of Service
Description:Authenticate user crashes, halts, stops or runs slowly; in all cases violating an availability metric.
Justification:Keycloak has no per-client or per-IP rate limiting. Set http-max-queued-requests (no limit by default) so the server sheds load, and rate-limit by client and source IP at the reverse proxy. Run at least two nodes.

131. Data Flow User credentials and client registration Is Potentially Interrupted  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Denial Of Service
Description:An external agent interrupts data flowing across a trust boundary in either direction.
Justification:If this flow is interrupted, no code, token, or session is issued, so the login fails closed and the user starts over.

132. Data Store Inaccessible  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Denial Of Service
Description:An external agent prevents access to a data store on the other side of the trust boundary.
Justification:If the store is unavailable, logins and token requests fail closed. Availability comes from database replication and a clustered cache.

133. Authenticate user May be Subject to Elevation of Privilege Using Remote Code Execution  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:Keycloak database may be able to remotely execute code for Authenticate user.
Justification:The process parses parameters and tokens with standard libraries and never evaluates input as code. Keep Keycloak and its Java runtime patched and run it as an unprivileged user.

134. Elevation by Changing the Execution Flow in Authenticate user  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:An attacker may pass data into Authenticate user in order to change the flow of program execution within Authenticate user to the attacker's choosing.
Justification:Redirect URI validation reads the client&#39;s registered URIs from this flow. Registered wildcards weaken it (RedirectUtils honors a trailing * as a prefix match), so the secure-redirect-uris-enforcer policy rejects them.
